newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Advance up after merger scheme cleared.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Advance up after merger scheme cleared.

text.p: The shares of regional bank Advance Bank Australia Ltd rose strongly in early Friday trade after a scheme for it to merge with fellow regional St George Bank Ltd was cleared by the Supreme Court of New South Wales on Thursday.
At 10.10 a.m. (2310 GMT), Adance shares were 12 cents or seven percent higher at A$7.15 on turnover of 508,987 shares.
By contrast, St George Bank shares opened weaker and at 10.20 a.m. (2320 GMT) were down 10 cents at A$7.54 on turnover of just 104,056 shares.
The share price moves of both banks reflected the increased likelihood of the merger being consummated, dealers said.
The final hurdle for the deal is the approval of Advance shareholders to alter the bank's articles of association at a meeting to be held on January 13.

Under the merger proposal St George Bank will offer Advance ordinary shareholders 0.625 of a new St George Bank ordinary share, A$2.10 in cash from St George and a 20 cent per share special dividend for each Advance Bank share.
Advance ordinary shareholders will also receive an interim fully franked dividend of 20 cents per share.
The offer values Advance at more than A$2.6 billion.
The biggest threat to the deal has been seen as National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB), which has a three percent stake in Advance and a 6.8 percent stake in St George.
"The non-approval of the scheme was the last wild card for NAB and their time to block the deal is fast running out," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Shaw Stockbroking.
NAB, which is seen as interested in buying regional banks, has not said whether it opposes the merger and did not appear at the hearing earlier this week.
